column1: # neurofedora real-data pipeline manifest
# Format (TAB separated, # = comment):
#   <pkg>
# Commands run with cwd = tests/, so use $FIX (the absolute fixtures dir)
# to reference fixtures portably. $TMP is a per-test tmpdir (auto-cleaned).
# Each row becomes a BATS @test that:
#   1. skips if <pkg> isn't installed (so partial installs are graceful),
#   2. runs the command,
#   3. matches <expected pattern> (POSIX regex) against combined stdout+stderr.
# Empty <expected> = "just require exit 0".
# A leading + on a pkg name means "skip if any of these alternative packages
# are missing"  (not yet implemented — placeholder for future multi-pkg pipes).
# Mark in-progress / known-failing rows with `# WIP:` to disable.
dcmtk
dcmtk
# Fedora ships the gdcm CLI in `gdcm-applications`, not the base `gdcm` lib pkg.
gdcm-applications
# gdcminfo encodes modality in the MediaStorage SOP-Class description,
# not as a standalone "Modality:" field
gdcm-applications
# teem 1.12 (COPR) rejects the NRRD0001 fixture format with "Couldn't init
# floatvector!?" even though it parses cleanly under teem 1.11. Dropping
# the teem pipeline tests until we can synthesize a fixture that teem 1.12
# accepts; the smoke layer still verifies /usr/bin/unu is installed.
# teem
# teem
# ─── ITK via SimpleITK (exercises InsightToolkit5 shared libs) ────────────────
python3-simpleitk
column2: python3 -c 'import SimpleITK as sitk; img=sitk.ReadImage("'"$FIX"'/t1.nii.gz"); print("shape=",img.GetSize())'

column1: # fsleyes render uses GLX even in headless mode — needs a real X display.
# We accept SKIP (no xvfb-run) or a successful render (file >= 1 KB).
python3-fsleyes
column2: command -v xvfb-run >/dev/null || { echo "SKIP: xvfb-run missing"; exit 0; }; out="$TMP/render.png"; timeout 45 xvfb-run -a fsleyes render -of "$out" "$FIX/t1.nii.gz" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; sz=$(wc -c <"$out" 2>/dev/null || echo 0); [ "$sz" -gt 1000 ] && echo "rendered $sz bytes" || echo "RENDER_EMPTY size=$sz"

# python3-vmtk currently FAILS at `from vmtk import vmtkscripts` with
# "ImportError: cannot import name 'vtkvmtk' from 'vmtk'" — the vtkvmtk C
# extension module is missing from the COPR build, almost certainly a
# VTK ABI mismatch (built against 9.5.x, current system has 9.6.x).
# Track as a real packaging bug; for now use a softer test that confirms
# the bare `import vmtk` works (which it does — vmtk/__init__.py doesn't
# touch vtkvmtk; only the vmtkscripts module does).
python3-vmtk
